Supercell's acquisition of Metacore expected to close this month
Once the deal is closed, Merge Mansion will officially become part of Supercell's live games portfolio.
Diego Argüello
,
Contributing Editor, News
,
GameDeveloper.com
September 3, 2026
2 Min Read
Image via Metacore
Supercell, the company known for the likes of
Clash Royale
and
Brawl Stars
, has signed a deal to acquire
Merge Mansion
developer Metacore.
The acquisition, which is expected to be completed at the end of September, is the latest example of major restructurings in the mobile game space. This deal itself comes as t
Metacore,
which restructured in May ahead the decision behind its own restructuring was to "better align with the core business, improve efficiency of operations, and respond to an increasingly competitive market environment."
According to comments from Metacore in May, its restructure and resulting acquisition by Supercell aims to "better align with the core business, improve efficiency of operations, and respond to an increasingly competitive market environment." This comes at a time where
Merge Mansion
's growth has "plateaued over the past few years" since its 2020 launch, as well when new investments have not succeeded in launching new games globally.

Once the deal is closed,
Merge Mansion
will officially become part of Supercell's live games portfolio. In the meantime, both companies are already working to plan the transition of the game.
"As we move into this next phase together with Supercell, I'm excited about the opportunities this creates for the game, our team and our players," Metacore CEO Mika Tammenkoski says in
this week's announcement
. "Supercell's expertise in operating and growing global live games over many years gives
Merge Mansion
the best possible foundation for long-term success."
The Next Phase of Metacore
The acquisition is just one part of what Metacore called "its next phase" back in May. At the time, uncertainty over
Merge Mansion's
future led to the company initiating change negotiations in Finland. According to information shared at the time, the studio would "consider reducing up to 160 roles" in the country if plans were to be realized.
Moreover, Metacore was also investigating "what kind of changes there could be" to operations in Germany and Sweden. None of these plans are mentioned in this most recent deal announcement. In addition, the terms of the transaction will not be disclosed.
"These are very difficult discussions," Tammenkoski said in the announcement back in May. "We have built an organization with growth ambitions that have not materialized as expected. The competition has become tougher every year since we launched
Merge Mansion
and created the 'merge 2' category as a pioneer. We need to make changes to remain competitive and to give
Merge Mansion
the best possible chance to succeed going forward."

Supercell, which sits under the Tencent umbrella, has spent the last couple of years
buying majority stakes in
and
acquiring studios
. In 2022, Supercell also ended development on two of its projects:
Clash Quest
and
Everdale
.
In April, the studio CEO and co-founder
received a BAFTA Fellowship
award in recognition of his long-standing contribution to the video game industry.
